whyThisShow: This is the last night of what one listener called "The Honey Year" — the run of shows from late 1973 into early 1974 where Jerry's guitar ran clean and warm, barely touched by distortion pedals [source: 'Most of the songs from Nov. '73 thru Feb. '74, however, sound like Jerry is plugged straight into the amp, with hardly any distortion pedals being used at all, except during the interstellar freak-out jams']. The Wall of Sound debuted at the very next show on March 23rd, so this Winterland date sits at a genuine hinge point in the band's evolution [source: 'Their live sound would start to change slightly after these Winterland shows; more rocking, with a somewhat heavier distortion in Jerry's guitar. I'm sure this has something to do with the Wall of Sound being unveiled at the very next show on 3/23']. One reviewer did flag that some listeners find the pace too restrained, so if you need the Dead at full throttle this may not be your first stop [source: 'I have noticed that some individuals have remarked that the pace is too restrained here']. But for heads who love the laid-back, jazzy side of the band, this whole February Winterland run is regarded as essential, and the 24th is one of its peaks [source: 'Get the whole run if you love the laid-back, jazzy, epic Dead'].
listenFor: The China Cat > Rider transition is a particular standout — the UJB-like segue jam drew one reviewer to call it "the best ever UJB-like segue jam" of that entire era, noting that "Jerry's tone is just crystal clear and in your face" [source: 'the best ever UJB-like segue jam is this 2/24/74 Winterland'] [source: 'Jerry's tone is just crystal clear and in your face...he really nails it with a special touch this night']. The Jack Straw also drew specific attention, described as one of the top five ever with licks that are "so f-ing smooth" [source: 'check out Jerry's brilliance on Jack Straw. This is in my top 5 Jack Straws...his licks are so f-ing smooth']. Row Jimmy stood out to one listener as "really slowed down and almost reggae like" with notable slide guitar work from Jerry [source: 'that row jimmy coming out of LIG is just amazing! really slowed down and almost reggae like, and how 'bout jerry's slide']. The Morning Dew closes the main set and is the performance that prompted one reviewer's most intense praise — they recommend listening with the volume high to catch the moments where Jerry "fizzles the notes away" at the end [source: 'Make sure that when you listen to the Dew you have it turned up loud. Jerry and the band bring this to a whisper and he fizzles the notes away'].
context: Recorded at Winterland Arena in San Francisco on February 24, 1974, this show falls squarely in the wall-of-sound era, though the Wall of Sound PA system itself had not yet been deployed — that happened at the next show on March 23rd. The recording circulates as a soundboard (identifier: gd74-02-24.sbd.windsor.199.sbefail.shnf) and was officially released as Dave's Picks Vol. 13. One reviewer rated it "the best sound quality for any 1974 show on this archive" [source: 'This is the best sound quality for any 1974 show on this archive']. The show is part of a celebrated Winterland run that included February 22nd and 23rd, all of which reviewers recommend getting together [source: 'find this along with 2/23 - both must haves'].
funFact: One listener described a recurring out-of-body experience while playing the Morning Dew in the dark with a candle lit, writing that their "spirit and soul is litterally transported back to 1974" and that they can "feel the energy" of Winterland — and specifically notes this happened "without LSD" [source: 'Many times I've had an out of body experience where (during the Dew) my spirit and soul is litterally transported back to 1974 and I'm in the Winterland Arena'].
headline: Last night of the honey year, Winterland, February '74.
